weeks.title: Approvals and ordering
weeks.exit_condition: Biosafety determination signed, genes ordered with a delivery estimate in hand, reagents ordered.

weeks.title: Transformation and stocks
weeks.exit_condition: Glycerol stocks frozen and labelled for at least wild type and R100K.

weeks.title: Thanksgiving, low intensity
weeks.exit_condition: Buffers and metal stocks ready, quantification method tested, and ideally one confirmed induced band.

weeks.title: Expression, lysis, purification
weeks.exit_condition: Purified wild type and R100K in hand, with a gel image proving it.

weeks.title: Assay, quantification, write-up
weeks.exit_condition: A quantified result, a figure, and a written interpretation ready to hand in the week of Dec 14.

tasks.title: Write one-page construct specification
tasks.detail: Host strain, vector backbone, promoter, tag, resistance marker, and the three inserts.

tasks.title: Note K-12 host, frame BSL-1 rDNA vs BSL-2
tasks.detail: Record that the host is a laboratory K-12 derivative and the work is recombinant DNA, so the question put to review is BSL-1 rDNA versus BSL-2.

tasks.title: Draft containment and decontamination section
tasks.detail: List segregation of transformed and untransformed cultures.

tasks.title: Meet supervisor, request written determination
tasks.detail: Present the construct specification and ask for a written biosafety level determination. Confirm which approval forms the fair requires and who signs them. Confirm the school holds a lab at the determined level and that supervision is available on the days the procedure needs it. Agree the date by which approval will be signed.

tasks.title: Order three genes, cloned into expression vector
tasks.detail: Order three genes each cloned into an expression vector, not as linear fragments. T7/lac promoter, N-terminal His-tag, resistance marker.
tasks.why: Gene synthesis is the one step that cannot be repeated inside the window.

tasks.title: Price express against standard tier
tasks.detail: Price the express synthesis tier against the standard tier and record both delivery estimates.

tasks.title: Confirm shipping to school address
tasks.detail: Confirm the supplier will ship to the school address, and whether an institutional account is required.

tasks.title: Place the full reagent order
tasks.detail: Competent cells, LB broth and agar, antibiotic, IPTG, lysozyme, Ni-NTA columns and buffers, NdCl3, CaCl2, native PAGE gels and buffer, stain, ladder, consumables.

tasks.title: Revise protocol to Phase 1 scope and submit
tasks.detail: Revise the protocol document to the Phase 1 scope and submit it alongside the approval forms.

tasks.title: Book lab access and supervisor for weeks 1, 3, 4
tasks.detail: Book lab access and supervisor availability for weeks 1, 3 and 4.

tasks.title: Confirm freezer availability and freezing method
tasks.detail: Confirm freezer availability and which freezing method week 3 will use.

tasks.title: Signed biosafety determination in hand
tasks.detail: The written determination, signed. Nothing is ordered until the biosafety classification is on paper.
tasks.why: This is the only annotation that can remove the December deliverable entirely.

tasks.title: Write the gel loading plan
tasks.detail: Lanes, conditions, ladder position, and which lanes carry the controls.

tasks.title: DNA received
tasks.detail: Placeholder date until the supplier's estimate is recorded (fork F2) and the actual arrival is logged (fork F4).
tasks.why: Gate at Nov 23 if DNA has not arrived.

tasks.title: Log receipt, check map and sequence, store at -20
tasks.detail: Log receipt, check the construct map and sequence file against what was ordered, and store the DNA at -20 C.

tasks.title: Confirm supervisor present for transformation
tasks.detail: Confirm the supervisor is present for the transformation session.

tasks.title: Transformation session
tasks.detail: Thaw chemically competent cells on ice and keep them on ice throughout. Add plasmid DNA to each aliquot; incubate on ice 30 minutes. Heat-shock at 42 C for 30 seconds, then return to ice for 5 minutes. Add recovery medium; shake at 37 C for 1 hour. Plate onto LB agar with the selection antibiotic, one plate per variant. Plate two controls: untransformed cells on antibiotic, which must show no growth, and untransformed cells on plain LB, which must grow. Incubate overnight at 37 C.

tasks.title: Read plates, check the negative control
tasks.detail: Colonies on the variant plates and none on the negative control plate means selection worked.

tasks.title: Pick two colonies per variant into liquid culture
tasks.detail: Pick two well-separated colonies per variant into liquid culture with antibiotic; grow overnight with shaking at 37 C.

tasks.title: Make and freeze glycerol stocks
tasks.detail: Make glycerol stocks from each overnight culture and freeze them.
tasks.why: This is the checkpoint that protects the rest of the schedule.

tasks.title: Autoclave plates and spent culture
tasks.detail: Autoclave all plates and spent culture before disposal.

tasks.title: Repeat transformation
tasks.detail: One repeat transformation fits in this week if no colonies appear. A second failure means the fallback decision moves forward to Nov 23.

tasks.title: Small-scale test expression
tasks.detail: One culture per variant, induce with IPTG, take samples before induction and after 3 hours at 37 C.

tasks.title: Denaturing gel on test expression samples
tasks.detail: Run those samples on a denaturing gel to confirm a band appears at the expected size.

tasks.title: Record the test expression result
tasks.detail: A visible induced band here removes most of the risk from week 3.

tasks.title: Prepare and label the five buffers
tasks.detail: Lysis, binding, wash, elution, native running buffer. Stable at room temperature or 4 C.

tasks.title: Prepare Nd3+ and Ca2+ stock solutions
tasks.detail: Prepare the Nd3+ and Ca2+ stock solutions, with goggles on, and label concentrations clearly.

tasks.title: Write and test the ImageJ quantification procedure
tasks.detail: Write the ImageJ quantification procedure and test it on a practice gel image so the method is settled before real data exists.

tasks.title: Draft results and methods, figures blank
tasks.detail: Draft the results and methods sections of the write-up with the figures left blank.

tasks.title: Prepare the Phase 2 outline
tasks.detail: Prepare the Phase 2 outline so it is ready regardless of how Phase 1 lands.

tasks.title: Inoculate overnight cultures from glycerol stocks
tasks.detail: Inoculate from glycerol stocks into LB with antibiotic; grow overnight with shaking at 37 C.

tasks.title: Grow to mid-log, induce, harvest, freeze pellets
tasks.detail: Dilute each overnight culture into fresh LB with antibiotic and grow at 37 C to mid-log density. Take a 1 mL pre-induction sample from each and keep it for the gel. Add IPTG to induce; continue shaking at 37 C for 3 hours. Take a post-induction sample from each. Harvest cells by centrifugation; discard the supernatant into disinfectant; freeze the pellets.

tasks.title: Lysozyme pre-incubation and three freeze-thaw cycles
tasks.detail: Resuspend each pellet in lysis buffer containing lysozyme. Incubate on ice 30 minutes to weaken the cell walls before the first freeze. Freeze: -80 C for 15 minutes per cycle preferred; dry ice and ethanol for about 5 minutes is an equivalent fast freeze; -20 C works but needs at least 1 hour per cycle. Thaw in a 37 C water bath until just liquid. Three cycles total. Centrifuge and keep the supernatant. Keep a small sample of the pellet for the gel, so an insoluble result is diagnosable rather than invisible.

tasks.title: Ni-NTA purification, keep every fraction
tasks.detail: Equilibrate the Ni-NTA column with binding buffer. Load the supernatant and collect the flow-through. Wash and collect the wash. Elute in small fractions, collecting each separately. Keep every fraction: if the elution is empty, the flow-through and wash tell you where the protein went.

tasks.title: Denaturing gel, confirm enriched elution band
tasks.detail: Run a denaturing gel with pre-induction, post-induction, soluble lysate, insoluble pellet, flow-through, wash, and elution fractions. Stain, image, and confirm a band at the expected size that is enriched in the elution lanes.
tasks.why: Without this, week 4 has nothing to assay - this is the second gate.

tasks.title: Estimate concentration, buffer-exchange if needed
tasks.detail: Estimate concentration, and buffer-exchange or dilute into the assay buffer if the elution buffer would interfere with the native gel.

tasks.title: First assay run, six samples
tasks.detail: Two variants x three conditions: protein only, protein with Nd3+, protein with Nd3+ plus a large Ca2+ excess. Keep protein concentration identical across all six - differences in loading look exactly like differences in dimerization. Incubate 30 minutes at room temperature. Load onto a native, non-denaturing gel alongside a native ladder; record the lane order before running. Run cold or in short bursts if the rig warms. Stain with Coomassie, destain, and image on a flat, evenly lit background.

tasks.title: Replicate runs two and three
tasks.detail: Repeat the full six-sample layout twice more from the same purified protein. Image each gel under identical conditions so band intensities are comparable.

tasks.title: ImageJ quantification, tabulate replicates
tasks.detail: Measure monomer and dimer band intensity per lane in ImageJ, subtracting local background. Compute the dimerization metric. Tabulate all replicates; do not average away a replicate that disagrees.

tasks.title: Spare day: repeat run or R100A assay
tasks.detail: Held for a repeat run if a gel failed, or for an R100A assay if that variant purified successfully.

tasks.title: Produce the dimerization figure
tasks.detail: Dimerization fraction by variant and condition, with individual replicate points shown.

tasks.title: Write results and interpretation
tasks.detail: State plainly what two technical replicates can and cannot support.

tasks.title: Attach Phase 2 plan and biosafety documentation
tasks.detail: Attach the Phase 2 plan and the biosafety documentation.

gates.question: Is the biosafety determination signed, and is it BSL-1?
gates.on_fail: BSL-2 means a BSL-2 facility with a qualified scientist, which is not achievable by December 14. Phase 1 becomes the computational fallback.

gates.question: Has the DNA arrived, and are glycerol stocks frozen for wild type and R100K?
gates.on_fail: Move to the fallback decision. Gene synthesis cannot be repeated inside the window.

gates.question: Is purified wild type and R100K in hand, with a gel image proving it?
gates.on_fail: Week 4 has nothing to assay. Fall back to the written interpretation of whatever gels exist, plus the Phase 2 plan.

options.label: BSL-1 - may proceed in the school lab

effects.note: Determination: BSL-1. In-school pathway stands.
Determination: BSL-2. Phase 1 becomes the computational fallback.

forks.question: Which synthesis tier did you order, and what delivery date did the supplier give?

effects.note: Express synthesis tier ordered.
Standard synthesis tier ordered.

forks.question: Which freezing method will week 3 use?

effects.note: Lysis: -80 C, 15 min per cycle.

options.label: Dry ice and ethanol bath, about 5 min

effects.note: Lysis: dry ice and ethanol, equivalent fast freeze.

options.label: -20 C only, at least 1 hour per cycle

effects.note: Lysis: -20 C fallback. At least 1 hour per cycle, three cycles. Lyses less completely; the lysozyme step partly compensates.
DNA received.

forks.question: Colonies on the variant plates, and a clean negative control?

effects.note: Selection worked.

options.label: No colonies - use the repeat transformation

effects.note: No colonies. One repeat transformation fits in this week.

options.label: No colonies on the repeat either

effects.note: Second transformation failure. The fallback decision moves forward to Nov 23.

forks.question: Do you have lab access on Nov 23-24?

options.label: Yes - run the small-scale test expression

effects.note: Lab access Nov 23-24. Test expression branch activated.
No lab access Nov 23-24. Preparation branch only.

forks.question: Was there a visible induced band at the expected size?

effects.note: Induced band confirmed. Most of the week 3 risk is removed.
No induced band in the test expression. Week 3 carries full expression risk.

forks.question: Is there a band at the expected size, enriched in the elution lanes?

effects.note: Purified protein confirmed on gel.

options.label: No - elution empty or no enrichment

effects.note: No enriched elution band. Check the flow-through and wash to find where the protein went.

options.label: Yes - R100A is available to assay

effects.note: R100A purified. Eligible for the spare day.
R100A not available. Spare day held for a repeat run.

forks.question: Did any gel fail? The spare day goes to a repeat before R100A.

options.label: Yes - use the spare day for a repeat run

effects.note: Spare day assigned to a repeat run.

options.label: No - use the spare day for the R100A assay

effects.note: Spare day assigned to the R100A assay.
Spare day not needed.
